findings.statement: Scope: this note covers only the bounded replay run:72cf0e4b91a3 (dataset sha256 72cf0e4b…, 55 events; 3 of 3 jobs completed; clink exit status 0; not cancelled; fan-in threshold 5 distinct senders in a 3,600,000 ms window; onward links allowed up to 1,800,000 ms gap). In this dataset there are 55 transfers, 48 accounts, 35 devices, 14 onward links and 2 fan-in alerts.

Alert fan_in:A-9278:1794301200000: account A-9278, event-time window 1794301200000 to 1794304800000, 6 distinct senders, 6 transfers, total 357,000 minor units. Contributing transfers: T0002 (A-4452, 42,000), T0003 (A-4366, 61,500), T0006 (A-7266, 38,000), T0010 (A-8133, 89,000), T0011 (A-6801, 50,500), T0012 (A-3881, 76,000). Each was sent from a different device.

Alert fan_in:A-9895:1794319200000: account A-9895, event-time window 1794319200000 to 1794322800000, 6 distinct senders, 6 transfers, total 15,000 minor units. Contributing transfers: T0035, T0036, T0037, T0038, T0039 and T0040, each exactly 2,500 minor units, from six different senders and six different devices.

Onward paths for A-9278: all six contributing transfers have an onward link. T0002, T0003 and T0006 each link to T0007 (A-9278→A-5092), then T0008 (A-5092→A-2897), then T0009 (A-2897→A-4989). T0010, T0011 and T0012 each link to T0014 (A-9278→A-5092), then T0015 (A-5092→A-2897), then T0016 (A-2897→A-4989). The longest path has 3 onward links. The path accounts are A-9278, A-5092, A-2897 and A-4989. Every path ends at A-4989, because T0009 and T0016 have no further qualifying transfer in this dataset.

Onward paths for A-9895: only T0038, T0039 and T0040 have an onward link, each to T0041 (A-9895→A-1415, 14,000). T0035, T0036 and T0037 have no onward link, so they start no path. The longest path has 1 onward link. The path accounts are A-9895 and A-1415, and every path ends at A-1415 because T0041 has no onward link in this dataset. A-1415's only recorded send, T0055 (90,000 to A-9514), falls at 1794333900000, 11,700,000 ms after T0041. That is outside the 1,800,000 ms onward gap, so no onward link is recorded, and T0055 itself has none.

Shared devices on paths: for the A-9278 alert, device D-568 sent transfers from three of its path accounts: A-9278, A-5092 and A-2897. All six onward transfers (T0007, T0008, T0009, T0014, T0015, T0016) came from D-568. A-4989 sent no transfer in this dataset. For the A-9895 alert, no device was used by two or more of its path accounts (A-9895 sent from D-699; A-1415 sent from D-785).
The only other device in the dataset used by more than one account is D-619 (A-9652 sent T0019, A-2952 sent T0027, both to A-5093). Neither A-9652 nor A-2952 is on either alert's paths.

What distinguishes the alerts: both have 6 senders and 6 transfers, so they look alike at the indicator level. The recorded relationships differ. (a) Amounts: A-9278 received varied amounts totalling 357,000; A-9895 received six identical 2,500 amounts totalling 15,000. (b) Onward coverage: every A-9278 contributing transfer has an onward link, but only 3 of 6 for A-9895. (c) Depth: A-9278's paths run 3 links through two intermediate accounts to A-4989, in two separate sequences; A-9895's paths stop after 1 link at A-1415. (d) Devices: A-9278's path accounts A-9278, A-5092 and A-2897 all sent from the same device D-568, while no device is shared on A-9895's paths. (e) Timing: on the A-9278 paths, the gaps between the onward transfers themselves are 140,000–195,000 ms. None of the downstream path accounts (A-5092, A-2897, A-4989, A-1415) has a fan-in alert.

hypotheses.statement: The A-9278 alert may reflect a coordinated pattern: several inbound credits, followed within minutes by repeated 3-step sequences of debits all sent from the single device D-568, with each step slightly smaller (138,000→135,000→132,000; 210,000→206,000→202,000). This is consistent with, but does not establish, one operator controlling A-9278, A-5092 and A-2897. The onward links record timing only; they do not show that the same funds moved, and a shared device does not show shared ownership or identity.

The A-9895 alert may be a more benign collection pattern, for example six people each paying an identical 2,500 contribution, followed by one later debit. Only half the credits have an onward link, there is a single shallow link and no device is shared, so the indicator alone is weak. This interpretation is not established by the data.

In arithmetic, T0007 (138,000) is close to the sum of T0002+T0003+T0006 (141,500), and T0014 (210,000) is close to T0010+T0011+T0012 (215,500). This could suggest aggregation at A-9278, but the dataset records only timing links, not the movement of funds.

unresolved.question: Who owns or operates device D-568, and are A-9278, A-5092 and A-2897 controlled by the same party? The dataset records device use only, not ownership or identity.
What happens at A-4989 and A-1415 after the paths end? The paths end only because no qualifying transfer exists in this bounded dataset; activity outside it is unknown.
Did A-9278 or A-9895 have credits or debits outside this replay that would change the alert windows or the onward links? The run record covers only the 55 events processed.
What was the purpose of the six identical 2,500 payments to A-9895, and of the debits from A-9278? The dataset has no transaction descriptions or counterparty relationships.
